name: Gochujang Beef Bowls with Smashed Cucumber Salad
description: Ground beef caramelized hard in a hot skillet and glazed with gochujang, served over jasmine rice with a cold, garlicky smashed cucumber salad. Fast enough for a weeknight, different enough to be worth the trip.
ingredients: 1 tsp toasted sesame oil (for the salad)
instructions: Rinse the jasmine rice until the water runs mostly clear, then cook with the 2.25 cups water — boil, cover, low heat 15 minutes, rest 10 off the heat.
Make the cucumber salad first so it can chill: lay the cucumbers on a board and whack them with the flat of a knife or the bottom of a pan until they split. Tear into rough 1-inch pieces.
Toss the cucumber pieces with the 2 tsp salt and let them drain in a colander for 15 minutes. Squeeze gently, then dress with the rice vinegar, sugar, minced garlic, and sesame oil. Refrigerate.
Whisk the gochujang, soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, and sesame oil in a small bowl.
Get a large skillet very hot over medium-high with the neutral oil. Add the beef in a flat layer and don't touch it for 4 minutes — you want a hard brown crust, not gray crumbles.
Break the beef up, cook 3 more minutes, then drain off most of the fat, leaving about a tablespoon.
Add the garlic and ginger, stir 30 seconds, then pour in the sauce. Cook 2–3 minutes until it thickens and coats the meat.
Serve over the rice with the cold cucumber salad on the side or right on top, finished with green onions and sesame seeds.
tips: Gochujang brands vary a lot in heat. Start with 2 Tbsp, taste the sauce before it hits the pan, and add from there — especially with kids eating.
Not touching the beef for those first 4 minutes is the whole difference between this and taco meat. Give the pan time.
Salting and draining the cucumbers keeps the salad crunchy instead of watery. Don't skip the 15 minutes.
Leftover beef is good cold, straight into a lettuce wrap or over rice for lunch.
